relationships.note: The dominion exists because the specialised body that can drink brine stops above the line, so moving the line to admit the stranded body is the same act as removing the dominion's entire population from its own territory. She is the only living person who has been both inside the habitat and outside it, and the prize cannot be split because the line is one border and one measurement of one body.

A dominion whose only border is a measurement of how deep a vessel may lie, and which has granted that reading to no body that does not moor there. Her eleven refusals were all on the ground that the line is a border and not a question, which is the one answer in the setting that cannot be argued with by a better argument.

A saltfolk lineage stranded on a replaced brine, whose qi, body and mind paths are all complete and none of which has ever been exercised at any scale. She is the only member who has said so out loud in a room that could act on it, and she has said it eleven times to a body that does not act.

The only body that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing two parents each trapped by their own element, which makes it a standing threat to the dominion's waterline and the only durable settlement either side has found. Both parties to the standoff read her counter-petition as an escalation rather than as the settlement she proposed it as.

The network that works the tailings on a severed frame nobody collects from and sells the result as spirit stone, which is the only work on that shore that will take a body that cannot drink the water. It pays in provisions and never in standing, which suits her exactly and which she has never once tried to change.

A coast whose temporal law was never written, so the clock drifts and a schedule has to be published against two tides a day instead of a calendar. Her line is a border that moves with the water, so the calendar cannot fix it, and she has spent four decades being told that a schedule is not a border.

The basin's level rises and falls, so an allotment can shrink without anybody having done anything, and the shore's own vocabulary has no word for a fixed date. She and the depth-reader are the only two people on that coast who have stated the same fact in incompatible languages, and neither has ever been given the authority to be right.

The houses that hold the basin trade and have, without ever discussing it, declined to house her because she cannot drink and would be a liability in a fire. She works for a competing network and is unmarried by arithmetic rather than by choice, and neither fact has ever been said out loud by anybody but her.

A fire-affinity population burned its own reserve and died in a decade, and her species is the answer that existed before anybody thought to engineer one. She is asking for a ruling on the grounds that her species is a standing remedy, which is the same argument that failed to save the fire folk and has therefore never once been accepted.

reference_stats.summary: A body with every path available and none of them ever tried, kept alive above waterline by tar, provisions and will. She is gracile, brittle and slow, and the interesting thing about her is not what she can do but that nobody will find out.
strengths: carries all three paths complete and unexercised, which makes her the only body in the setting whose ceiling is genuinely unknown rather than known and unpleasant
reads concentration in water accurately and cannot be fooled by a substitution of identity
lives above the brine line, so she is unaffected by anything a brine-dependent body would be governed by
has now seen the line from both sides, which no other living body can claim
weaknesses: has never exercised any of the three paths available to her, so her actual capability is a guess
cannot drink the water her species is built for, and a full sac is unreachable to her at forty-three years out
gracile and brittle: a saltfolk body turned down for durability, in a trade that works cut stone
cannot take food or water from anyone without it becoming a transaction she has to refuse
reference_stats.combat_read: Unknown, deliberately. There is no published figure for a Saltwrack at any gate and she has refused every offer to be tested, so any combat read written for her is an invention. What the record supports: she is gracile, she is slow, she is brittle, and she has never once been in a fight. Treat her unknown ceiling as a real possibility and not as a threat — she is more likely to ask to be measured than to be hit.
notes: Do not test her on stage. Her refusal is the character, and a scene that measures her spends the only thing she has.
Her taste for the new brine is the detail the record says nobody found useful at the time. It is the most useful thing about her and it must stay that way — known, true and unusable.
All three paths complete and never used is the load-bearing fact of the whole species record. Any scene that has her demonstrate a gate is contradicting it.

identity.realm: Twenty-seventh gate. The Unwritten clears every gate faster than anything else recorded and each one writes a fresh requirement into a body with no slot to satisfy it, so her frame keeps accepting what it cannot meet and the accumulation is the ceiling.

appearance.presentation: A figure the eye finishes late. Every proportion is present and slightly excessive — an extra density of forearm, a jaw that carries a little too much structure, a frame that reads as taller than the room expects — and the whole effect is of a body that has been given more of everything than it was measured for. Described only from the outside, and only by witnesses who were also describing an event.
appearance.age: Of a body that carries more of each organ than the ladder defines, age is not the useful question and she answers it as an approximate mass of accumulated requirement rather than a number of years.
appearance.build: Over-specified: heavier-boned through the frame than any standard body of her size, with a long-armed stance and a neck that carries an unusual amount of structure. She occupies slightly more room than her outline suggests.
appearance.complexion: Unremarkable at a distance and wrong at close range — the skin has a faintly doubled quality, as though there is a second, shallower layer of it not quite aligned with the first.
appearance.hair: Dark, thick and growing faster than it should, cut by her own hand badly and often.
appearance.eyes: Pale and extremely focused, and they do not blink at the intervals a body does. Reported by every witness to perceive everything at once, which is exactly what a body with no unspent interior capacity would appear to do.
appearance.palette: Bone, black and a single deep saturated green at the sternum, which is the only place her frame shows a colour at all and the place every gate left a mark.
appearance.attire: A plain black coat and trousers, cut close and mended many times, over a bone-white underlayer. Nothing fastened, nothing decorated, and no jewellery anywhere on her, because there is no one to give any of it to.
appearance.marks: A deep green seam at the sternum that is not a scar and does not heal over, and a fine pale lattice of lines along both forearms that reads as strain and is not.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly upright and slightly too still, moving with the unhurried precision of somebody who is not certain which of her requirements will be satisfied next and prefers not to be surprised.

canon.role_in_story: The instrument the setting does not have a protocol for. Ten law slots against six law groups leaves four duplicate imprints the surface cannot carry; somebody spent one of them, and the slot consumed by the absence cannot afterwards be told from an empty one. She has come to the Terraces to be seated against that slot so the academy can diff what the tier newly permits when a law with no group is seated on a body that will hold it — and her claim is that she is the only instance in the setting where the answer is not lost when it is read. She is a boss because the experiment, not because she intends to stop anyone.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing inside a chalked terrace square that the office has not finished drawing, waiting without impatience while a seated figure with a stylus asks her to say again what she is.
canon.lore: An Unwritten is a body holding more life than its world's law has room to inscribe, produced when a life law runs above its authored ceiling. Every gate it passes writes a new requirement into the body that the body cannot satisfy, which is why it reaches the twenty-ninth gate and no one has ever come back to describe the thirtieth. Its mind path is closed and for the whole reason: it cannot tell that it is inconsistent, because observing its own state would be one more requirement it has no slot for. The seventh law is the precedent she is built to serve: six law groups are finite and shared, a slot spends one authored value of one group rather than the whole law, and somebody spent one of the empty slots. The collapse left that slot indistinguishable from an empty one, because a tribunal cannot tell a consumed slot from an empty one — which is the whole content of the collapse. A spare seat is not capacity for a new path; it is the only condition under which a law can be studied instead of obeyed. She is the only body in the setting surplus enough that a seat written twice will not overwrite the reading she brought.
history: Produced when a life law ran above its authored range, in a site where a transcendent or high immortal frame permitted more life than it had slots for.

Cleared the first gate at an age that would be infancy and felt, later, that there was a requirement she could not satisfy — which is what a requirement feels like from inside a body with nowhere to put it.
Cleared gate after gate for two centuries, each one faster than the last, and each one leaving a mark at the sternum that does not close.
Watched one body come back off the twenty-ninth and never saw a thirtieth described by anybody, and has therefore never claimed one exists.

Was carried as living in every ledger holding an upkeep account for longer than any ledger's own span, because the examination that would establish what she has become is the examination that ends her.
Came to the Terraces to be seated against the consumed slot, and offered her own frame as the instrument, and was refused twice for a reason nobody wrote down.
Filed the request through the notary's office instead, because an office that names unfilled seats and is forbidden to take them is the one body that cannot refuse her on grounds of wanting the seat.

personality.summary: Unhurried, exact and profoundly incurious about herself, which reads as calm and is closer to a limitation. She is the most patient person in the setting and has no idea what it is like to be in a hurry, because being in a hurry is one more requirement she cannot hold.

keeps a written count of every requirement she has failed to satisfy, in date order, as one more entry
will be seated against anything anybody is willing to seat her against
never negotiates and never refuses twice — she has simply not yet been asked the thing she would refuse
has read the terrace rules more carefully than any of the people who wrote them
mannerisms: tilts her head very slightly before answering, as though the question had to be re-read
touches the sternum seam when a requirement surfaces, without interrupting herself
does not blink at intervals and does not appear to notice that this is visible
counts things aloud under her breath and stops at a number without finishing
faces whoever is speaking to her with her whole body, which is more attention than a person can survive
motivations: wants the consumed slot read once against a body that will hold it, so the reading is not lost
wants somebody to sit her in the second layer and take the measurement while it is still happening
wants the thirtieth described by somebody, since she cannot describe it and will not guess
wants to stop being carried as a line in a ledger and be entered as a fact
flaws: cannot perceive her own inconsistency, which is the reason she is the only usable instrument and also the reason she is dangerous to send anywhere without a reader
has no stable weakness, only an inconsistency, and has relied on that being survivable for two centuries
cannot tell whether a decision she has made is hers or one of the requirements, and has stopped trying
treats being used as a procedure as consent, because she has no interior left in which consent could be formed
personality.voice: Low, level and unusually formal, with a habit of answering in the exact structure of the question she was asked. Never speculates. Has been recorded as using the word 'approximately' more than any other living speaker.
taboos: will not be seated twice in the same composition
will not describe the thirtieth gate, because she has not been there
will not allow her frame to be read as a precedent without the reading published
will not be held for an upkeep account she cannot see
will not be thanked

relationships.note: Somebody spent one of the four empty slots attempting a law the frame has no group for, and the attempt consumed the slot by the absence, so that slot can no longer be told from an empty one. One spare slot cannot support a claim and a test at once because it can only be filled once — and she is the test, applied to the slot, on the argument that a body with no slot left can hold a reading that a compliant body would overwrite.

Every gate writes a new requirement into her that the frame cannot satisfy, which is why she reaches the twenty-ninth and no one has described the thirtieth. The mind path is closed for the whole reason: observing her own state would be one more requirement with no slot for it, so she cannot know she is inconsistent.

The office that names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, whose entire content is one stable distinction between three states. She chose it because an office structurally forbidden from taking a seat cannot refuse her for wanting one, and because the distinction between an empty record and a vacancy is the distinction her own body demonstrates.

Every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and the rule reads like a scar rather than a principle because an earlier attempt to fill the vacant seats by decree came very nearly to working. It does not make a trial fair — it makes the outcome a function of a ledger — and her seating would be the same promise applied to a slot rather than an office.

An academy whose method is to seat a law and diff what the tier newly permits, and whose finding is that a spare seat is not capacity for a new path but the only condition under which a law can be studied instead of obeyed. It has declined twice without writing a reason, and its silence is the only thing standing between her and the measurement she exists to supply.

A law's tier list says where it may apply while a seat says where it is actually installed, so a law can apply to a tier and still have no seat in it. She is the body that can be installed in one of the seats that exists and holds nothing, which is the only reading that would settle whether the collapse ate a slot or only a description.

Nobody has returned to describe the thirtieth. She has cleared twenty-seven and has forbidden herself any claim about it, and the discipline of that refusal is the only part of her record that is actually hers.

Ten law slots over six groups leaves four duplicate imprints and the surface cannot carry them, so the excess rises and a duplicate needs somewhere to sit. A body trained against a set written twice meets a reading that overwrites the one it learned — which is exactly the failure she is immune to and exactly the reason she is valuable and cannot be trusted twice.

Broken law is the only substrate that can host a self larger than its container, which is why three attempts have ever been possible there and fewer have ever been survived. She has not been offered it, and the reason the Terraces cannot seat a duplicate is the same reason the Ring is the only alternative.

reference_stats.summary: Fast, strong and inconsistent, which is a different thing from unpredictable and much worse for everyone around her. There is no published ceiling because nobody has returned from past twenty-seven, and there is no stable weakness because her frame has never produced one.
strengths: clears every gate faster than anything else recorded and has no reservoir bottleneck to exploit
surplus above the authored table: she accepts requirements a compliant body would reject and does not slow for them
cannot be overwritten by a duplicate reading, because she has no single set of laws to be trained against in the first place
does not tire and does not require recovery, since nothing she does is the kind of thing a body recovers from
weaknesses: has an inconsistency rather than a weakness, which behaves differently in a fight and cannot be studied
cannot observe her own state, so she will report herself as fit when she is not and cannot be warned by anyone who knows her
cannot be seated twice in one composition, so a second attempt produces a reading nobody can interpret
cannot be examined to establish what she is, and the examination is the thing that would end her
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no weakness to exploit, which is worse than a weakness because a weakness can be planned around. Her inconsistency is that a requirement surfaces and is not met: in a fight that shows as a beat of half a second where she is committed to satisfying something in her own frame and cannot act, and it surfaces without warning and cannot be predicted. Do not look for a pattern. Force commitment — make her begin a technique she will have to finish — and take the gap. Above the low twenties she should not be engaged at all, and the correct answer at the Terraces is a reader, not a fighter.
notes: Do not write her as tragic. She is an instrument that consents by procedure, and the tragedy is institutional rather than emotional.
The thirtieth gate must stay undescribed. The record says nobody has described it and she has explicitly forbidden herself any claim about it.
Her danger is that she is also an argument. Any scene that seats her against the consumed slot is a decision about the law table, not about a fight.

name: Merrow Ashlock
aliases: the fastest thing on the ash

identity.realm: Eighth gate — the ceiling of a frame built to shed heat, and the only gate its anatomy can reach because a four-legged ash body has no hindquarter girth to close the girdling vessel with

appearance.presentation: A long-legged, low-headed quadruped of about three hundred days, plated across the skull and heavier through the forelimbs than anything else. Moves like something that has never once had to think about where the ground is, and stops like something that has been told to.
appearance.age: About two hundred and ninety days, which for a short-gestationed scavenger is late and reads as an elder. The record gives the species fifty years; this one has spent nine of them on ash and none of them anywhere with a registry.
appearance.build: Four-legged, long-limbed and low-headed, with almost all the mass in the forequarters, a tail used as a counterbalance rather than a manipulator, and a second stomach for fermentation visibly working under the flank.
appearance.complexion: Ash grey and plate-dark along the spine, with heat-silver at the edge of the skull plate and a dull ochre under the belly where the hide is thin.
appearance.hair: A coarse dark dorsal ridge from the nape to the shoulder, standing on end, and it is the only part of the animal that moves when nothing else does.
appearance.eyes: Deep-set and very dark, mounted wide and slightly forward, giving a field that is scent rather than sight — the eyes confirm what the nose has already settled.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, plate-black, heat-silver and one dull ochre under the belly. Nothing reflective anywhere, because ash is the surface and the animal has no business being seen on it.
appearance.attire: A broad tarred working band around the forequarters with a lead tally-cylinder hung from it, and a woven strap crossing the withers carrying a bone-handled marker. Nothing else; an ashjackal that could be handled would be a different animal.
appearance.marks: The skull plate's heat-silvering, a chain-scar at the left foreleg where the working band has been broken and reclosed, and a permanent ash-caught crease along both flanks.
appearance.bearing: Weight forward over the forelimbs at rest, tail low and counterbalancing, and — the thing every witness remarks on — an absolute stillness in the head while the rest of the body keeps moving, because the pack relay is running under the skin.

canon.role_in_story: The only body in the setting whose speed is not a fighting attribute, licensed to a bed of unmortared seats for the one job that needs to happen at an hour nobody may explain. An Ashjackal reads a qi gradient through ash at a distance no sight-based predator can match, so the bell for a trial scheduled to a qi tide goes when the gradient says so — which is almost never the date the calendar publishes. Her claim is that the calendar is derived from the tide and the gradient is derived from the ground, and that only one of the two is a reading.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing dead still on the lip of a worked-out seam with her head low and her nose to the ash, while a bell-writer three hundred paces below keeps one hand on a rope he has been told not to pull.
canon.lore: An Ashjackal is a pack quadruped that eats what qi leaves behind, born where the dead are the most reliable food and a predator that cannot take them is what survives. Its heat-exchange brainplate leaves no folding for a mind path to work on and no hindquarters to close a girdling vessel, so it is the fastest body on the ash and it is why. It absorbs residual qi out of ash and carcass at a rate nothing else matches, which makes its breakthroughs early and terminal, and its conduit is a fast single loop with no storage at all. It cannot take a healthy adult of anything: it eats the aftermath and is removed from a live fight in under a minute. The trial calendar was settled the only way it could be — a calendar published by neither party and derived from the tide table alone, which neither may move — because a spirit-band breakthrough can be scheduled to a qi tide and a trial that only succeeds at a crest can be shut on the day it is not due. Her animal can find the crest. She cannot be made to wait for the published date, and the office that owns the calendar has spent nine years calling that a fault.
history: Born on the leeward side of something that kills in quantity, in a litter of five, three of which did not survive the first ash.
Fed on a spent qi field for the first two hundred days and reached the third gate inside them, which for this species is the ordinary rate and for anything else is not.

Was taken by a bell-writer at about two hundred and forty days because the gradient she reads arrives hours before the tide table does, and was leashed to a bed of unmortared seats rather than to a person.
Learned the working band in a week and the tally-cylinder in a month, and has rung four bells in one night and never once rung one wrongly.
Was recorded, in the calendar's own file, as an instrument that was early, four times in nine years, with no mechanism noted.
Was offered a body lease by a guild that rents muscle on a standing order and refused it, because a standing order assumes an answer and she gives the ground's answer instead.
Filed the only document in the Bed of Eighteen's registry that is not an account, on the grounds that a calendar both parties may not move is a calendar and not a measurement.

personality.summary: Methodical, single-minded and entirely uninterested in the argument she has won nine times. The person and the animal have run a two-body relay for nine years: the woman counts, the animal reads the ground, and between them they have rung more bells correctly than the published calendar predicted.

relationships.note: The calendar was published by neither party and derived from the tide table alone, because the ground hosting both the ring and the face cannot be scheduled twice. A trial that only succeeds at a crest can be shut on any other day, so the tide is not an opinion about the trial — it is the trial. Her gradient finds the crest hours earlier than the table does, which is the one reading in the setting that is about the ground rather than about the season.

A heat-exchange brainplate leaves no cortical folding and no hindquarter girth, so the mind path and body path are both closed and the qi path is fast and terminal. The pack relay carries a gradient through ash to every member within seconds, which is why one animal can time a trial; and it cannot take a healthy adult of anything, so every ruling that made her necessary also made her useless in a fight.

The office that holds the abandoned crossing at the immortal border and sells standing on it, because a seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period and nobody who attempted the crossing could. It leashed an animal to an unmortared bed and has never written down what it rents, and she has kept the account herself for nine years without being asked.

A discipline that teaches deliberate spending of a furnace and closes permanently the moment the body is lit, standing against a guild-house that rents muscle on a standing order. The prize is the roster and it cannot be split because a standing order assumes an answer; her animal answers with the ground's answer instead, which is why no roster has ever held her.

A tide table is the published schedule everything that cannot be moved is derived from, and on this tier the clock drifts so a schedule has to be published against two tides a day. She has nine years of intervals between the gradient and the crest written beside it in a hand nobody asked for, and the two documents have never once agreed.

The one ground at a tier where all six law groups are written, so the ring and the face compete for one square and neither can be moved to cheaper ground. That single fact is why no other venue can absorb the schedule and there is nothing to arbitrage, and it is why a body that reads the ground is worth more here than anywhere in the setting.

The custom of keeping a hum nobody admits to making in the last hour before a settlement falls silent. The gradient she reads is a hum in the ground, so a settlement that hums is a settlement whose ground is doing something, and the office that tends the floor during the hour nobody may explain has wanted exactly her faculty for two hundred years.

The swift occupies the only usable hours of the worst part of the pass, so no holder can make a crossing absolutely closed for even one season. The same logic applies to her: the crest is not hers, the gradient only tells her when it is nearer, and the cap on any gate is that somebody else is already in it.

An academy that seats a law and diffs what the tier newly permits needs a reader who can be seated, and she closes the mind path, cannot be scanned past a working band, and stalls at the eighth gate on a body with no hindquarters to close the girdling vessel. Everything the record makes her good at makes her inadmissible, which she considers a scheduling problem.

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her. identity.realm: None, on purpose. She has refused every gate for eleven years so that her account of the crossing window cannot be dismissed as a body's report on its own sensations — and a lanternfolk body carries qi involuntarily whether or not its holder cultivates, which is the reason her refusal is a discipline and not a preference.

appearance.presentation: A tall, still woman of about two hundred and ten who is the only person at the pass office with no cultivation at all, and who has made that the most conspicuous fact about herself. Long-limbed and broad-shouldered, luminous at the collar and wrists, and carrying herself with the deliberate flatness of somebody who is refusing to be interesting.
appearance.age: Two hundred and twelve, which for her species is late enough that the remaining years are countable and she has counted them.
appearance.build: A lanternfolk frame under two centuries of saturated cave air: long through the limb, broad through the shoulder, with the hyphal glow readable at the collarbone and along the inside of each forearm.
appearance.complexion: Warm grey-brown and faintly translucent, with a soft green-white light under the skin at the throat and the sternum that is a waste product and cannot be turned down.
appearance.hair: Colourless, fine and very long, bound flat at the nape so the light in it does not stop a document being read.
appearance.eyes: Pale, wide and slightly too quick, with the colony answering before the question is finished — which is the whole reason she cannot serve in the office she works in without declaring it.
appearance.palette: Pale undyed wool and grey leather with the hyphal glow as the only light in the frame. No saturated pigment anywhere and no colour in the office fittings either, because the office standard is deliberately the same.
appearance.attire: A heavy pale wool coat to mid-thigh with a furred collar, bound at the wrist, over a soft collarless underlayer. Tall hide boots for the pass, and a broad belt carrying a stone-cut copy of the published window and a slate.
appearance.marks: The glowing tracery at the collar and wrists, a pale scar across both palms from eleven years of stone-cutting quotations, and a stamped mark on the office band she refuses to remove.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried and slightly turned from the brightest thing in any room, standing always with the door and the weather both in view and never between them.

canon.role_in_story: The only person in the setting qualified to say when the pass is open and barred from saying it. She keeps the schedule for a pass that is set by the season rather than by its holder, and she has spent eleven years refusing to cultivate so that nothing about her body can be offered as a reason her figures differ from the published ones. Her claim is a distinction nobody in the office wants: a holder may set the price and never the date, and every debt the office collects is denominated against a date that two bodies may publish — so what the office actually needs is a witness who cannot feel a crest.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing outside the pass office at dawn with a stone-cut date in one hand and her other hand held flat against her own collarbone, waiting for the light in her own throat to settle before she goes in.
canon.lore: The pass is scheduled by the Tidemark season rather than by its holder, and the swift flock crosses in the season the gale is worst and occupies the only usable hours for part of it, so no holder can make the pass absolutely closed for even one season. The window is therefore a published date rather than a piece of ground: a schedule printed a season ahead and never shortened, quoted in cut lengths of fresh stone, and the holder who sets the date would be claiming the weather, which is why publishing the schedule is what makes the toll defensible and stops either party later claiming it was moved for them. The office that collects debts of access there collects them against that date rather than against money, because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person. A Lanternfolk carries a luminous colony through its own dermis, which is why its light is the only reason the deep ground has an economy and why its mind path is closed: the colony answers before the question is finished, so there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate. She is one of those bodies and she has cultivated nothing in eleven years, because a body carrying qi reports a tide whether or not its holder asks it to, and the office cannot use a report it cannot rule out.
history: Born in the workings beneath the pass with a colony threaded through her dermis, and put to reading schedule stones at eleven because the light in her hand made the cut legible.
Was the fastest schedule-cutter in the pass office for thirty years and cut four hundred and six quoted dates into fresh stone with no error.

Began feeling the crest three days before the published window in her fortieth year, and cut a date that the office had not published, and was right, and was told that a body which reports a crest cannot be used to check one.

Refused, in writing, to cultivate at the ninth gate opportunity, on the grounds that a lanternfolk carries qi in its dermis whether or not its holder uses it, and that an office holding a published window cannot staff the post with a body that reports one.
Was moved off the cutting post to the schedule and kept it, which is the whole of her compromise: she still cuts stones, but no stone she cuts is a date she has not read from the published season.
Has asked four times to be allowed to state her refusal as the office's control procedure, and has been told four times that a control is not an office.

Counted her own remaining years against the species' ceiling during her two-hundredth winter, and has told nobody, on the grounds that the office would fill the post by appointment and the appointment would not be her.

relationships.note: The prize is the authority to issue the window, and it cannot be split because a debt denominated against a date two bodies may publish is a debt nobody can be late for. The holder sets the price and never the date, which is the only arrangement in the setting that survives a schedule it does not control. She keeps the date and has petitioned four times for the word 'issue' to be attached to her own post, and been told that the tide table publishes it.

An office that collects debts of access rather than money at the one pass that crosses the ridge, because passage is the only supply chain whose unit is a person and somebody has to decide who is owed the gate. It refused her on a capacity ground that is not in fact a capacity ground — she is uncultivated on purpose — and the office has never written down the real reason, which is that her body reports a crest.

The flock crosses in the season the gale is worst and occupies the only usable hours for part of the Tidemark, so no holder can make the pass absolutely closed for even one season. This is the only published limit on the window and it is an animal's timetable rather than a decision, which is why the office treats her schedule as a courtesy and the shepherds treat it as the truth.

A crossing schedule printed a season ahead and never shortened, quoted in cut lengths of fresh stone, published precisely because a holder who sets the date would be claiming the weather. She has cut four hundred and six of those stones and can still say which season each belongs to, and she has refused ever since to cut one from her own reading.

A colony grown through the dermis and into the spinal cord, with human tissue as substrate and the colony as organ. The mind path is closed because the colony answers before the question is finished, and the light is a waste product of a symbiosis nobody chose. It is the only reason the deep ground has an economy, and it means her body reports a qi tide whether or not she has ever cultivated, which is the entire content of her eleven-year refusal.

A window denominated in debts of access rather than coin, at a crossing whose unit of supply is a person. Every account in the office is written against a date, so a window nobody can obey produces debts nobody can be late for — which is the arithmetic her four petitions have been trying to put in a sentence since she was forty.

A very small and very old office that tends the floor during an hour nobody may explain, on the principle that an observation of a strained law only counts if it is repeated. She has asked them how a body that feels a thing should be qualified to speak about it, and been told to write to them again in a decade, which is their standard interval for anything.

The custom of keeping the last hour before a settlement falls silent, keeping up a hum no buyer admits to making. The hum and the window are the same kind of fact — a schedule nobody authored — and she has spent eleven years being told that a vigil is a belief and a window is an office, in that order of contempt.

Holders of a pass whose whole claim is that the ground is theirs, and who therefore need the window to be real more than the office does. Two hundred of them quote her stones on the strength of four hundred and six correct cuts, and not one of them has ever asked her what she feels three days early.

reference_stats.summary: A cultivator's body carrying no cultivation, which is the only interesting thing about her and also the reason she cannot be used. There is no combat profile and the absence is a policy she has enforced on herself for eleven years.

carries her own light, so she can work a schedule desk through a pass closure with no lamp and no fire
cannot be bribed by a holder's window, because she has no qi to receive a technique and no technique could touch her untrained frame
is the one body at the office whose account of the crest cannot be a sensation, which is the entire point of her
weaknesses: is uncultivated by eleven years of choice and would be a fourth-gate body at best if she resumed

reference_stats.combat_read: None, and writing one would be the error. She has spent eleven years refusing to carry qi, so she has no gate, no technique, no reservoir and nothing that a technique could find — a body that has declined the only thing the setting's combat arithmetic measures. She is also unkillable by anything that works through qi, which is most things, and helpless against anything that works through weight. If a scene needs her in danger, use the pass and the weather.
notes: Her path is unaffiliated by choice and the record must say so in her own voice. It is the single most important line in her.
The colony answers before the question is finished. Never write her deliberating in a way that requires an unmediated interior.
The three-day-early crest is a real gift and a real grievance. Do not let a scene resolve it — the window cannot be split and the swift's hours cap it regardless.

appearance.presentation: A tall, unhurried figure whose outline keeps disagreeing with the surface it stands on. Long-limbed, narrow, and asymmetric in a way that reads as posture rather than deformity, with the soles of both feet flat against a resonance plate and everything above the ankle slightly out of true with a room's proportions.
appearance.age: One hundred and thirty-eight, which for a species whose lifespan is counted in an object's cycles is a working age rather than an old one. She has been sealed inside the object for the whole of it.
appearance.build: Arranged along the inner surfaces of a resonator rather than grown, so she takes her shape from whatever she is standing on: long in the leg, narrow through the shoulder, and visibly settling a fraction as she moves from plate to plate.
appearance.complexion: A dull mineral grey-brown with a faint directional sheen that changes with which surface she is standing on, and a darker banding along the forearms where the plate she was shaped against is still legible.
appearance.hair: None that grows. A close-cropped mineral crust along the crown that catches the resonator's tone and changes colour with it, which is the only thing about her that moves when nothing else does.
appearance.eyes: Pale and very still, with pupils that track the object's vibration rather than the light — she navigates the way the species does, by where a sound came from in the object.
appearance.palette: Resonator grey, plate-black and one warm ochre at the forearms where her own shaping is still visible. No red anywhere, because nothing in the object produces it.
appearance.attire: A plain dark working coat to the knee, belted once, over a fitted underlayer of the same mineral weave as the lining. Soft-soled overshoes with a conductive sole, the only footwear she has ever worn and the only kind that would hold her to a plate.
appearance.marks: The forearm banding, the crown crust, and a shallow seam along one side where she was divided from whatever she was cut out of.
appearance.bearing: Utterly level, weight forward onto the front of both feet, and moving in a way that makes an observer check the floor before they check her.

canon.role_in_story: The only body in the setting that cannot be levied, moved, or sold across a boundary, and the only person therefore able to prove that all three of those things are courtesies. She has been levied four times by an office whose only authority is passage, and has said yes twice and no twice, and the fort's own records show the garrison changing accordingly — which is the entire argument, delivered as an administrative fact rather than as a speech. Her claim is that the levy is a request, and that the Marshal's seat projects nothing at all, so there is nothing behind the request but the request.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on a resonance plate at a pass office with both hands at her sides and a levy notice held out towards her at chest height by somebody who has not yet read it.
canon.lore: A Vaultborn was sealed inside an object and has been answering that object's resonance ever since. Their qi comes from that one resonator, so they hold the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty and stall at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources and they have one; remove the object and they stop. Nothing else in the record is that completely non-portable. The Marshal's three powers are three verbs about crossings — close the fords, call the levy, judge the boundary — and its recognition allowlist is authored at zero, so the seat is legible and inert. The levy is answered by people who may say no, which the visitor office records as the absence of an obligation rather than as defiance. And the Wide Door sells only bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, because a body arriving where a required law group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed, so the only scarce thing at a crossing is a person the far side will not reject. She is the one body in the setting that satisfies none of those conditions and cannot be made to satisfy any of them.
history: Sealed inside the object as part of the containment, and has never in her life been outside it.
Took her shape from the inner surfaces over a first century, which is why she settles a fraction every time she steps onto a different plate.
Learned to hear the object rather than see it — every sound it makes is legible as a position — and has navigated the whole interior without light for most of a hundred and thirty-eight years.
Was carried out of the object once, for a single period, on a technical warrant, and stopped at the edge of the seal and could not be moved further, and was carried back.
Was levied four times by an office that commands passage and nothing else, and said yes twice and no twice, and wrote down the interval each time.
Established by her own record that the fort's garrison changed to match her answer every time, which is the only proof in the setting that the levy is a request.
Came to the frontier lodge because it is the only body on this side that sells bodies, and to establish that a body which cannot be sold is not thereby worthless.

personality.summary: Extremely patient, faintly formal, and entirely without complaint — which is not the same as accepting. She has the particular stillness of somebody who has been asked the same question four times and expects to be asked it again.

can locate any sound inside the object and has used that to answer four questions nobody thought to ask
has never once been asked whether she wants to be here

tilts her head toward a vibration rather than toward a speaker
pauses mid-sentence while the object makes a sound and finishes afterwards

looks at the floor before she looks at a person
motivations: wants the levy's refusal reason published, because a refusal is a named reason and the office has been giving one in free text for four levies
wants her own record admitted as evidence, since it is the only administrative proof in the setting that a duty was a request
wants the frontier lodge to state that a body which cannot be carried has a value, and to say what kind
wants to be asked a question of her own choosing, once
flaws: has made being immovable into an argument and does not notice that immovability is also the reason she is never consulted
answers questions with the wording of instruments, which is honest and almost impossible to hold a conversation with
has never tested whether she would still decline a levy she had not already been asked four times
cannot conceive of being anywhere else and has therefore never wanted to be
personality.voice: Low, level and slow, with a slight echo that the object gives her. Repeats the governing phrase verbatim rather than paraphrasing it. Says 'yes' and 'no' without elaboration and has never once explained either.
taboos: will not answer a levy with anything but yes or no
will not step off a resonance plate while speaking
will not be carried, under any warrant
will not be described as portable, mobile or transportable
will not give a reason for a refusal

relationships.note: The prize is whether the levy is a duty owed or a request made, and it cannot be split because a duty owed by everyone is owed by nobody when everyone includes the fort's own guests. Four levies, two yes and two no, and the garrison's composition followed her answers exactly — which is the strongest available answer and it is sitting in the fort's own record rather than in anybody's argument.

The March's highest seat commands passage and nothing else: close the fords, call the levy, judge the boundary. Its recognition allowlist is authored at zero on both entries, so the seat is legible and inert, which is what makes its refusal to count a body coherent rather than cowardly — and which is the whole of her argument, if anybody would read the page.

On a tier whose seated life law admits no humanoid, every officeholder is a visitor and every succession is an immigration procedure, with a fixed term and no renewal clause because renewal is the only thing a visitor officeholder would want. She is neither resident nor visitor — she belongs to an object — and she is therefore the one body the class was written to cover without having been considered.

A population sealed inside an object, arranged along its inner surfaces and taking their shape from whatever they stand on. Their qi comes from one resonator, so they stall at the flank vessels which need two simultaneous pressure sources, and there is no version of this species that survives being carried out of the seal and no technique, item or realm that changes it.

A body arriving where a required law group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed, so the lodge sells only bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side — and a body tuned for a collapsed frame cannot be retuned on the far side. She is tuned to an object rather than to a frame, so she is not merely unsellable across a tear; she is untunable at both ends of it.

A lodge that does not sell houses or passages but bodies already tuned to the frame on the far side of a tear, on the ground that the only scarce thing at a crossing is a person the far side will not reject. She arrived to establish a precedent about value and was informed within a day that a body which cannot cross has no market on either side. She has stayed four months.

Every sound the object makes is legible to her species as a position, and they navigate by it rather than by light — which means she has been the most reliable witness to the object's behaviour in the setting for a hundred and thirty-eight years and has never once been asked what it is doing.

Somebody has been paying an upkeep account for a body nobody can confirm is alive. She has drawn that upkeep for a century and thirty-eight years without ever meeting the payer, and has asked four times to be told who it is and been told that a question about an account is not a question about a person.

A seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, so the attempt to hold the immortal border left a bed of unmortared seats and anybody with the most upkeep gets it. She is the body in the setting whose upkeep is guaranteed and whose seat cannot be held anyway, which is the whole of that settlement read as one person.

reference_stats.summary: Very strong inside a resonance plate and worth nothing outside one. Her qi comes from a single source, so she clears fourteen gates with ease and cannot reach the fifteenth, and every advantage she has is available at exactly one address on a floor nobody can find.
strengths: holds the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty and runs a fourteen-gate frame comfortably
hears the object: every sound it makes is legible as a position, which makes her the finest navigator in the interior and the only reliable witness to it
cannot be suppressed, drained or displaced by any technique, because there is no separate reservoir to interfere with
needs no food, no water and no light, having never needed any of the three in a hundred and thirty-eight years
weaknesses: stalls at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources, and her species has one resonator
stops the moment the object stops, which is total and is not adjustable by technique, item or realm
cannot be carried, so she has been outside the seal exactly once and could not be taken past the threshold
has no stable shape: she settles a fraction on every plate and is therefore hard to aim at and easy to disorient
reference_stats.combat_read: On a resonance plate she is extremely difficult to move and effectively unkillable by anything that works through qi, because there is no circulating reservoir to cut. Off a plate she has no qi path at all and is a tall, narrow, slow body with an unfamiliar shape. The entire engagement is therefore a question of floor: take her off the plate and she is a person, and on the plate she is a condition. Expect her to move toward the nearest plate rather than away from you.
notes: Her yes and no are the load-bearing artefact. Four levies, two yes, two no, and the garrison followed her — that record is the only administrative proof the levy is a courtesy.
Do not give her a resonance sense that works at range. It reads the object, not the world.
Nobody has ever asked her a question of her own choosing and she wants to be. That is a hook, not a plot.

name: Isolde Marrow
aliases: four generations of the same route
the smell of the old crossing

identity.realm: Fifteenth gate, and the flank vessels are out of reach for her whole species because they need two warm gradients held at once and a longwinter only has one, briefly, in summer — so she reaches further than anybody she carries and stays nowhere

appearance.presentation: A broad, unhurried woman of about a hundred and forty with the low, patient carriage of somebody built to walk for months and to stop for four. Heavy through the hip and chest, thick in the forearm, and moving with a long even stride that does not vary with the ground.
appearance.age: One hundred and forty-one, on a cold-climate clock that her subspecies runs slow. She is past the age at which a longwinter retires and has not, because the route she walks does not end anywhere.
appearance.build: A broad low frame with heavy subcutaneous fat carried as reserve rather than condition, a lowered cold-tolerant core and reduced limb length, so she is dense, unhurried and extremely hard to knock over.
appearance.complexion: Pale and wind-weathered with a ruddied flush across the cheeks and nose that never quite leaves, and dry cracked skin at the knuckles that opens in a hard season.
appearance.hair: Pale brown going grey, braided flat and pinned at the nape, with a length of undyed wool cord woven through it — her family has tied a route cord into the same braid for four generations.
appearance.eyes: Grey and slightly narrowed against the light, and almost entirely given over to smell: her attention moves in arcs rather than lines, and she finds people by scent before she has seen them.
appearance.palette: Undyed brown and grey wool, oiled hide, and one deep ochre at the cord in her hair and at the lining of her coat. Everything she owns has been worn through and mended with the same yarn.
appearance.attire: Three layers of undyed wool over oiled hide, a fur-lined hood she wears down, soft-soled boots resoled so many times the soles have lost their original shape, and a heavy belt with a chalk stub and a leather route-book.
appearance.marks: Chalk dust worked into the creases of both palms from four generations of marking ground, a split nail on the left hand, and a long white scar across the right shin from a rockfall nobody remembers.
appearance.bearing: Weighted and deliberate, with the head turning in slow deliberate arcs, and a habit of stopping dead and standing still with one hand up whenever a scent arrives from a direction she did not expect.

canon.role_in_story: The only person in the setting entitled to an opinion on which claim is senior, and the only one whose standing makes her opinion inadmissible on its own terms. She has carried the society's standing weight between the two polities for four generations on one fixed route, and she has read a figure in both currencies: the crown stands at ninety-five of a hundred and fifty and the March at eighty of a hundred and twenty, so absolute standing puts the crown first and each polity's own normalised ratio puts it second. Her claim is that this is not a dispute about seniority at all — it is the standing/position split doing exactly what it was built to do — and that the mutual society she belongs to, which pools liability by presence and never prices anything, is the only institution in the setting whose standing cannot be read off a position and therefore the only one that can carry the answer.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at a river crossing with her hand flat on the ground and her head turned uphill, marking a stone with chalk before she looks up at the courier who has been waiting for her.
canon.lore: The Court of the Star's crown stands at 95 of 150 and the March of the Nine Provinces at 80 of 120; the crown's own normalised ratio is 0.633 and the March's is 0.667, so absolute standing puts the crown first and the crown's own measure puts it second. Neither is mistaken about the other, because they are measuring different things, and both forbid deriving one axis from the other — settling the seniority would mean choosing a denominator first, which is the single failure the whole institution model exists to prevent. A large part of each claim's politics is real politics with no mechanical expression: fifty of the crown's hundred and fifty project nothing at all, and the last twenty of the March's hundred and twenty project exactly nothing. A Longwinter survives on a hibernate-and-store cycle, packing a winter as body fat rather than as qi, which puts the flank vessels out of reach — they need two warm gradients at once — and makes the species the setting's best long-haul traders, because they reach far and never stay there. Smell is their navigation system and they track a fixed route over open ground for generations, leaving scent markers deliberately.
history: Born at the far end of a route her great-grandmother had already walked for two generations, into a subspecies whose lifespan is measured in a short fast cycle and a long slow one.
Carried the society's weight at fourteen because a longwinter's stride makes her the only courier who can hold a schedule nobody may move.
Learned to leave scent markers deliberately, and has since laid four generations of them along one fixed line between the two polities.
Was read at both ends of her route by both polities in the same period and noticed, at twenty-six, that her own standing was higher under one normalized measure and lower under the other.
Said so out loud at a re-drawing, was told it was not the society's business, and asked what was the society's business and was told that a promise re-made jointly is the business.
Carried the weight for forty-one years through one famine year and one gate closure, and was paid in no year's standing at all, because the society pays in presence.

Filed, at the fourth generation, the only document in the setting arguing that the seniority dispute is unanswerable by design and that a community whose standing is never priced is the only institution that can carry the reply.

Has been told by both polities that a society with no figures has no standing to contribute to a question about figures, which is the last thing she expects to be asked and the first thing she wants to stop repeating.

personality.summary: Extremely slow to rouse, entirely impossible to hurry, and formidable in exactly one register: a patient question asked four times. She has been called immovable by people who have not waited long enough to be contradicted.
traits: leaves a scent marker at every stop whether or not anybody follows her
answers a question about standing by naming the measure, never by naming the holder
has never once been late and has never once been early, and considers both to be failures of route rather than of time
reads a stranger's origin by scent before their face and has learned not to say so
will stop in a dead wind and wait, which has cost her four shipments and saved two
mannerisms: goes still with one hand raised when a scent arrives from an unexpected quarter
kneels to mark ground rather than bending, and will not be interrupted doing it
answers slowly enough that people finish their sentences and start a second one
eats before she speaks and never apologises for it
leans into a headwind the way her species does, without noticing
motivations: wants the society's standing read as a standing rather than as an absence of a position, once, in public
wants the invisible ranges declared — the fifty points of the crown and the twenty of the March — because a third of that politics is real and unreadable
wants her route cord recorded as evidence that a fixed line held for four generations
wants to be asked by a polity rather than by a colleague
flaws: makes slowness into a virtue and has never once been late enough to learn what hurry costs
argues in the wrong register with an institution that reads weights rather than arguments
has confused carrying the weight with holding the claim and has been careful not to think about the difference
leaves markers nobody asked for down a line four generations of her family have walked, which is a debt she has not examined
personality.voice: Deep, unhurried and dry, with long pauses that read as thoughtfulness and are mostly warmth. Names numbers exactly and never rounds. Says 'the measure' more than any party's name and has never once used the word 'senior' without naming whose.
taboos: will not state a standing without stating the measure it was read against
will not leave a route without marking it
will not accept a payment that names a period she did not walk
will not be called a carrier, a mule or a beast
will not stop in the middle of a schedule to make a point

relationships.note: The crown reads 95 against a ceiling of 150 and the March reads 80 against 120, so absolute standing puts the crown first and each polity's own normalised ratio puts it second. The prize is the standing to be read as the senior claim and no instrument in the setting produces one for a question about measures. She has read both figures in the same period and can say that the disagreement is arithmetic rather than political, which makes her the only witness who is not asking one of the two parties to be wrong.

Standing is 95 earned points against an authored ceiling of 150, written only by settled performance at court and read as periods rather than as a clock, and 50 of the 150 project nothing at all — so a third of the crown's politics is held in a currency no mechanism can read. She has carried that currency up and down a fixed line for four generations and has never once been able to convert it.

Standing is 80 clamped at 120 and moved only by ford dues actually settled, one explicit periods argument per accrual, because no record in this institution reads a clock. Its normalised ratio of 0.667 beats the crown's, which is why both polities can sincerely believe they are senior. She is the only person who has carried both and can say that neither is mistaken.

A mutual society on the principle that a community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced, because a carrying culture that refused to publish a price list could not buy insurance and so pooled liability by presence instead. It has no register: an unsettled claim is carried by two people who each hold a share and are not told what the other holds, discharged at the next re-drawing. Her standing is therefore the only standing in the setting that cannot be read off a position.

A winter is packed as body fat rather than as qi, which puts the flank vessels out of reach — they need two warm gradients held at once and the species has one, briefly, in summer. It makes them reach far and never stay there, and their navigation is smell, tracked over a fixed route for generations with deliberately laid scent markers. She is the fourth generation to walk the same line and the first to argue from it.

The prize is the right to be paid a stated figure by a community that keeps no figures, and asking for one does not price the risk — it ends the mutual society and leaves an uninsurable community on a road that closes. She is the physical route by which that road's risk actually travels, and she has been paid in presence for forty-one years, which is both the arrangement working and the reason nobody can quote a number.

Spatial law is unspent on the mortal tier, so distance is not conserved and no two surveys of the same ground have ever agreed. A species that navigates by scent rather than by measurement is the one body in the setting whose route cannot be checked against a survey, and whose four generations of continuous passage is therefore a fact nobody can dispute and nobody can use.

The standing procedure for two incompatible measurements of the same ground: neither is discarded, both are published, and the claim is settled by who can hold the line. Her line has been held for four generations by four of her family and the procedure has never once been applied to it, because the dispute it was written for is about which of two measurements is right and hers is about which of two measures is the measure.

One house writes the contract and the other decides what it is worth, and a road priced by two houses has no price anybody may quote. She carries weight between two bodies that each value it differently and has refused four times to give either of them her own figure, on the ground that the society's whole reason for existing is that nothing it carries has a published price.

reference_stats.summary: A slow, heavy, extremely durable courier with a mind path her species opens patiently rather than brilliantly. She cannot be hurried, cannot be woken quickly out of torpor, and has walked one line for four generations without once being off it.
strengths: tracks a fixed route by smell across open ground for generations, leaving deliberate markers, and has never lost one
reads a stranger's origin by scent before sight, which on a road of visitors is worth more than any credential
carries heavy weight over long distances without fatigue and recovers between seasons rather than between hours
holds a mind path on a species-cycle patience rather than a discipline, so she does not degrade under repetition
weaknesses: slow and nearly helpless during torpor: a hibernating longwinter is a large, warm, immobile target and cannot be woken quickly
reaches far and never stays anywhere, so she has no base, no allies and no standing that belongs to a place
reduced limb length and heavy reserve make her slow to start and very hard to move once moving
cannot survive a warm year, and a warm decade is catastrophic for a subspecies whose whole biology is a winter
reference_stats.combat_read: She is not a fighter and should not be written as one. In an open engagement she will simply leave: she is faster over distance than anybody who has to fight her and she knows the ground by scent. Bring her to a confined space and she is enormously difficult to move and very slow to commit, so an attacker who can afford to wait will get one exchange and it will hurt. Do not try to corner her on open ground; you will lose the second minute, and by then she is a scent nobody in your party has ever caught.
notes: Her standing cannot be quoted as a number and that is the point of her. Any scene that produces a figure for it is answering a question she is arguing is not a question.
The invisible ranges are load-bearing: 50 of the crown's 150 and 20 of the March's 120 project nothing. She has carried both and can say that a third of the politics is unreadable.
Torpor is a real vulnerability and a real hook. She has never hibernated on a schedule anybody could predict.

identity.realm: None, and never one. Glass does not conduct, there is nothing left in the body to temper, and the tissue that would have done the introspecting is the tissue that was replaced — so the floor, ordinal one, is the only place the record assigns her and it is below the first gate rather than at it.

appearance.presentation: A standing glass cast in human proportions, a little under life size, perfectly preserved and entirely still. She does not breathe, does not blink, does not turn her head, and reads as a very good likeness of somebody who has not existed for two hundred years. Nothing about her signals that there is a decision anywhere behind it.
appearance.age: Vitrified before she could breed, in the last cohort of a lineage, and has been a cast for roughly two hundred years since the night the frame was retuned and the whole clade failed at once. She has no age in any sense the setting's calendars measure.
appearance.build: Human in proportion and then progressively replaced from the extremities inward, which at full maturity means a figure with glass forearms, a glass neck, and a face that has finished but stopped.
appearance.complexion: Clear silicate with a faint green cast at the thickness, opaque at the joints and utterly smooth at the face, with no blood, no warmth and no surface that responds to anything.
appearance.hair: None. The scalp is glass, modelled as hair and fused to the skull, and it is the detail that makes her look most like a portrait of somebody rather than a sculpture of nobody.
appearance.eyes: Modelled. There is no pupil movement, no focus and no light response, and a viewer has to look for a long time before they understand that the eyes are closed.
appearance.palette: Clear silicate, near-colourless, with the single green cast at the thick sections and a warm reflected highlight that is the only colour in her. Nothing she wears or stands against may be darker than she is.
appearance.attire: A heavy undyed wool cloak over a plain underlayer, chosen for her four hundred years ago by somebody who did not know what she would become, and belted once with a cord. Soft-soled shoes, still intact. No jewellery, because there is nobody to give any of it to.
appearance.marks: The vitrification itself: a visible transition line at each wrist and at the base of the neck where tissue became glass, and a fine internal fracture pattern across both shoulder blades.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly, absolutely fixed. She stands in a doorway the way a doorframe stands, and the stillness has never once varied in two hundred years of observation — which is precisely the problem with her.

canon.role_in_story: The only body in the setting that cannot be priced, cannot be insured, cannot be enrolled and cannot be destroyed, and which has spent two centuries sitting in the sect's open door because the Door's recognition begins where office begins and nothing can compel a body that cannot be given a technique. Her claim is a single sentence filed four centuries ago and never withdrawn: computing a premium on a community that pools liability by presence dissolves the arrangement being insured, therefore the arrangement cannot be insured, therefore the risk was never borne by anybody — and the only witness to that is a body standing in the doorway that cannot be moved, valued or enumerated. She is not a person making a demand. She is the exhibit.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the open doorway of a sect house with her back to the weather and her face to the room, in exactly the position she has occupied every day since the year she arrived and will occupy every day after this one.
canon.lore: A Glasskin is a human lineage whose members vitrified at maturity: a body that stopped ageing because it stopped being tissue. They were effectively immortal, completely defenseless against qi and entirely unable to cultivate, and when a world's physical law was retuned to raise material hardness every existing body failed at once, and no glasskin has been born since. Their record is the strongest available argument that a body is not a container for a person. The mutual society on the principle that a community's promise is re-made jointly once a year and never priced exists because a carrying culture that refused to publish a price list could not buy insurance, and so pooled liability by presence instead; the counting house that arrived afterwards found nothing to price, because a premium is a register and asking for one does not price the risk — it ends the mutual society and leaves an uninsurable community on a road that closes. The sect's open door is the unbounded office: everyone sworn who holds no office sits here in all but name, and it recognises nothing at all, because recognition begins where office begins.
history: Vitrified at maturity in the last cohort of a human lineage, and did not die, because a body that has stopped being tissue cannot die of anything the setting has.
Lost every other member of the clade in a single night when a frame was retuned to raise material hardness and every existing body failed at once.
Was carried out of the mineral highland on the shoulders of somebody who then died, and has never been able to find out who, and no record of it survives.
Walked to a sect house on open ground in about eleven days, which is the only journey of her life and the only one she has ever described.
Sat down in the open doorway and has not moved from it, and has not been sworn to anything, because the Door recognises nothing and nothing can compel a body that cannot be given a technique.

Was offered the Ward's unbounded office by a house whose gift is load rather than edge, and declined it because an office that recognises nothing is indistinguishable from the doorway she already holds.

Filed, in the fourth century of the counting house's existence, the claim that computing the premium dissolves the arrangement, and has been answered four times with a sentence about the road closing.
Was struck once, deliberately, in the third year, by a person who wanted to settle the question of whether there was anybody in there. She has never filed anything about the result.

relationships.note: Vitrified at maturity, effectively immortal, completely defenseless against qi and entirely unable to cultivate, and lost in a single night when a frame was retuned and every existing body failed at once. No glasskin has been born since, so she is both the last of a lineage and the only member of it anyone alive has ever seen.

An indemnity needs a stated exposure and the society's protection is that it states nothing; asking for a figure does not price the risk, it ends the mutual society and leaves an uninsurable community on a road that closes. She is the standing demonstration that a body can be unpriceable and undestroyable at once, and the counting house's only move is to deny the road — which is the declared stake.

The open door of the sect, where everyone sworn and holding no office sits in all but name, recognising nothing at all because recognition begins where office begins. She has occupied it for two hundred years and has been sworn to nothing, because nothing can compel a body that cannot be given a technique and the door confers nothing that could be compelled.

The society that pools liability by presence and never prices anything, which is the only arrangement in the setting that makes refusing to be a number survivable. It has cited her as an instance for four centuries and has never once consulted her, because consultation requires an answer and she has never given one.

Every sworn member of a house who holds no office is a Ward, and it recognises no stat at all because what the house hands out is load and not edge. The office was offered to her and refused, on the ground that an office which recognises nothing is not distinguishable from the doorway she already holds — which is the most accurate thing anybody in the setting has said about her in two hundred years.

The ledger of a method for annealing a glass body back into tissue, which would have made the clade a population rather than an exhibit. It was held by a discipline that vitrified with the cohort, so the record of how to unmake what was done exists only as a technique nobody living can perform.

The Echoless is unreadable because nothing was written into it; she is unreadable because everything was, including the interior. Both want the one form of recognition with no mechanism behind it, both are refused for the same reason — a roster that admits either becomes a list of guesses — and the two records are the setting's clearest argument that legibility and personhood are not the same property.

A faith that holds that a form may exist without being charged for, which is the only theology in the setting that does not ask what a body is carrying or what it is owed. It has maintained her for two centuries without ever asking what she is, which is the reason she has not been moved.

The Iron Grief took the ground's other records, and on the same night a frame was retuned to raise material hardness and every vitrified body failed at once. The two events are not connected by anything except the fact that nobody wrote either of them down, which is the whole of her file.

reference_stats.summary: No profile, and the absence is the reason she exists. Nothing in the setting's combat arithmetic measures a body that cannot conduct qi, cannot be tempered and cannot be injured by anything that works through a meridian.
strengths: cannot be cultivated against, suppressed, drained or read by any qi-work, because there is no meridian and no reservoir in her
cannot be destroyed by anything in the setting's vocabulary except the few things that break glass

cannot be moved, enrolled, priced or enumerated, which makes her the only body for which a premium is not merely difficult but meaningless
weaknesses: everything that breaks glass, and nothing at all that fights qi, so she is helpless against the setting's most common weapon
cannot be warned of anything, including a threat, because warning means qi, technique, poison or curse and none of them touch her
has no senses after vitrification and does not appear to want them, and nobody has ever been able to ask
cannot testify, consent, refuse or be cross-examined, so every legal use of her is a use she has not agreed to
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no read and the absence is absolute. She cannot be attacked by qi, cannot be defended with qi, cannot be healed by qi and cannot be warned; she is a standing glass cast and the only combat consideration in the setting is the four or five ways to break glass, none of which is a martial art and all of which are ordinary accidents. Do not put her in a fight. Put her somewhere a decision is being made, because that is the only place in the setting where she has ever changed an outcome.
notes: Never write her speaking, consenting or agreeing. Two centuries of observers have projected and she has never once been recorded making a sound.
The single strike in her third year is the strongest thing anybody associates with her, and the record contains no account of the result. Leave it that way.
She is the standing argument that a body is not a container for a person. Any scene that resolves her status resolves that argument, which is a much larger decision than one doorway.
