appearance.presentation: A slight, quick woman of about fifty-eight with the plain look of a working clerk and the one gift nobody expected: she sees. Her parent glows; she does not, and in a room lit only by a lanternfolk the only thing anybody can see is her.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight, which for a subspecies that lost two hundred and fifty years at a stroke is old. She is the oldest person in any lanternfolk settlement and has never once been treated as an elder rather than as an anomaly.
appearance.build: A lanternfolk frame with the colony gone: narrower through the shoulder than her parent, fine-boned, lighter and colder than anything that lives in the ground, with the fragile wrists and long fingers of a body that stopped being repaired.
appearance.complexion: Cool and faintly grey, with a fine silicate shimmer along the forearms and a translucence at the temples where the mineral bloom replaced the hyphae. Nothing about it is warm and it is the only thing about her that reads as unusual in a lit room.
appearance.hair: Colourless and fine, cut short, and unlike her parent's it does not glow at the ends — which is the single fact about her appearance that a settlement identifies her by.
appearance.eyes: Pale and wide and genuinely effective in darkness. The most-cited difference from the parent and the reason the subspecies is named for it, and the reason she is the only person underground who can read a document.
appearance.palette: Grey and bone and the deep green of her parent, all of it muted by the absence of light in her. One accent: a cold white at the lattice on her forearms, which is not a mark and does not glow.
appearance.attire: A close grey work jacket over a soft collarless underlayer, sleeves bound, and a bone-handled stylus at her belt. Soft-soled shoes, because she cannot leave the cave system either and has stopped pretending the work clothes imply otherwise.
appearance.marks: The silicate lattice in place of the hyphae, a fine shimmer from the fingers to the elbow on both arms, and a pale scar at one temple where a mineral bloom reached further than it should have.
appearance.bearing: Quick, light and slightly stooped from ninety years of reading by a lamp her own body does not make, with a habit of turning her face toward the darker part of any room.

canon.role_in_story: The living control case for the setting's one classification it cannot perform. The register reads the dead as the frame said, and the frame's only stated difference between her parent and her is a fungal colony that grows, occupies the interior, and can be replaced or lost — and hers has been lost, which is exactly what makes her the body on which that classification can finally be tested and exactly what disqualifies her from it. She has asked to be entered on the same page as her parent and been told twice that the register classifies by a temporary organ.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in a mortuary doorway holding a lantern at her own hip, reading a name off a frame plate by the light of a lamp that every other body in the building is producing involuntarily.
canon.lore: A Deadlight is a Lanternfolk whose fungal colony died and was replaced by a mineral bloom, which cost them the two hundred and fifty years and gave back the mind path. It is the control case: everything the colony did for them and everything it prevented, recorded on a body where both can be measured against the parent species. The bloom is inert, so nothing in it transacts with qi — which is why her qi path is complete but slower than her parent's — and nothing in it repairs anything, which is why the shorter life is authored rather than incidental. The colony's light is a waste product of a symbiosis nobody chose and the only reason the deep caves have an economy; she has the mind path her parent cannot have and the ninety years her parent would not have lost. The mortuary college's method descends directly from the door liturgy: you stand in the doorway, you are the light, and whatever is in the room is read by it. She is the one body in those buildings that is not a light, and she can read better than any of them.
history: Born into a lanternfolk settlement with a living colony and a hundred-and-fifty-year expectation, and was read at birth as a full member of the species.
Lost the colony between nine and eleven, in the way nobody has ever fully explained, and the bloom that replaced it is inert, cold and repairless.
Was found to see in the dark within a season, which the settlement named the subspecies for and has used ever since as though naming were an explanation.
Watched her parent's span compress by a hundred and sixty years in her own body, and has kept the only written record of the change because nobody else writes anything down.
Was tested for the mind path at nineteen, passed the first gate that her parent has never been able to attempt, and stopped there because the bloom repairs nothing and a gate costs.
Was refused admission to the mortuary college twice on the ground that the register reads the frame and the frame says the difference between her and her parent is an organ that dies.
Was entered in the household register as an anomaly in her twenty-fourth year, on the frame's own reading, and has asked twice for it to be amended to a person with a life.
Is sixty-eight in the bloom's own count of the settlement and ninety in the settlement's count of the body, and has asked which of those belongs on the page.

relationships.note: The prize is whether either body may be entered in the register as a person with a life, and it cannot be split because the frame distinguishes the two by a colony that dies — so a register classifying them apart is classifying by a temporary organ. She is the population that classification was written about, standing in the room, alive, and she is the reason the classification is testable and the reason it fails.

A lanternfolk body with a silicate lattice in place of the hyphal colony: lighter, colder and entirely inert, with the body grown around what replaced the fungus rather than recovered. The bloom holds qi where a colony transacted with it, so her qi path is slower and complete, and nothing in this body is being repaired — which is why the ninety years are authored and not a matter of luck.

A colony grown through the dermis and into the spinal cord, which is why the species reaches two hundred and fifty and closes the mind path: the colony answers before the question is finished. Their light is a waste product and the only reason the deep caves have an economy. She has the mind path and cannot stay; they can stay and cannot introspect; and neither of them can do both, which is the finding the subspecies exists to record.

The college that keeps the burnt list, reading the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers. Its method descends from a door liturgy in which the reader is the light — and she is the one body in its buildings that is not a light and reads better than any of them, which makes her refusal the most embarrassing one in its history.

The practice of standing in the doorway as the light and having the room read by you, built on the fact that a threshold is the edge of a law budget and the world will not promise welcome. She has the access and not the light, which means she can stand in any doorway in the deep ground and be read by nothing at all.

Every sworn member of a house who holds no office is a Ward, and it recognises no stat at all because what the house hands out is load rather than edge. She holds a Ward's place on the only terms available to her body — no office, no recognition, no measure — and it is the only institution underground that has ever entered her without calling her an anomaly.

Coffins recorded but never opened, and a register that counts them. She can read frame plates in the dark, which means she is the only person in the settlement capable of opening one to check, and she has argued that a register which counts an unopened coffin is counting a reading rather than a person.

A body repaired by nothing stops costing less and less over a life, and she has measured her own gates at one, four and nine and then stopped, because a gate costs and this body does not replace what a gate spends. Her record of her own slowing is the only longitudinal data on bloom-body decline anybody has kept.

The cleft's moss maps the jade gradient and dies back over any cut ground, so cutting the jade is also grazing the only map of where the seam runs. Her parent cannot leave the caves for the same reason and by the same mechanism, and the two of them are the reason the exchange below ground keeps working without a record.

Expect her to fight badly and read perfectly: in darkness she will know exactly where you are, what your qi layout is and where your gate stops, and she has four gates of throughput to spend on it. In light she is a slow, brittle, ninety-year-old woman with excellent eyes. Bring the fight to a lit room or bring qi she cannot see, and do not try to outlast her — nothing in her repairs, so she also has nothing that can be worn down further.
notes: She is the control case. Every argument in the record that compares her to her parent species runs through her, and she is alive and present for all of it.

identity.realm: None, and the reason is arithmetic rather than temperament: a technique is a subscription and cultivation needs eleven consecutive periods in one place, and she has never spent eleven periods anywhere, because her work is a single crossing and her body only works where two kinds of water are both within reach

appearance.presentation: A wiry, sun-browned woman of about seventy-eight with the look of somebody who has been caught between two climates her whole life and has stopped needing either. Narrow, quick, and permanently dusted at the collar with a white salt bloom she has given up washing off.
appearance.age: Seventy-eight, which the cross matures slowly and reads as middle, so she has been taken for forty older on four continents and has never corrected anybody.
appearance.build: A saltfolk frame gone gracile and then trained narrow: deep through the chest, long in the forearm, and light enough that a full day's crossing costs her nothing.
appearance.complexion: Weathered tan, pale at the collarbone and the hairline where the salt comes through the skin, and permanently damp-looking at the cuffs because she is wet to the elbow twice a day.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cropped for wind, and lighter than it was at forty because the salt has taken it.
appearance.eyes: Grey-blue and quick, sitting behind the best chemical sense in the setting. She looks slightly too long at everything, and is not being rude.
appearance.palette: Bone white, wet slate and tar black, with one deep blue at the collar that is the only dye she owns and that no longer takes.
appearance.attire: A tarred canvas coat to the thigh, waxed trousers, a salt-stiff belt with two stoppered jars clipped to it — one of which is always full and one of which is always empty — and boots resoled so many times they have lost their shape.
appearance.marks: Salt bloom at the collarbone and hairline, split nail beds from rope, and a permanent white line across each wrist where the water reaches.
appearance.bearing: Weight on the balls of the feet, ready to move in either direction, and habitually positioned with the door and the road both in view — the stance of somebody whose profession is crossing and whose complaint is that crossing is charged twice.

canon.role_in_story: The counterexample the gate-fee dispute has been waiting four hundred years for. She has been sold the same crossing twice — once as a place in an order of arrivals and once as a price for that order — and her claim is not that the toll is high but that it is counted twice for one body. Her position is the watch's own asymmetry: the watch may not keep a bead or a standing, so it has nothing to lose in a ruling, while the brokers keep everything and are judged entirely on their own record. She is the only body on the tier that can cross between the two chemistries, and she is the only person who has ever been charged for both halves of the same crossing.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at a stair-foot gate with two stamped slips in one hand and her other hand flat on the ring wall, holding both up at the same height for the broker to look at.
canon.lore: The watch decides the order arrivals are served in and the brokers decide what that order is worth, and both sell the same visitor. The prize is one price for one admission, and it cannot be split because gate fees are the only tax ground that cannot measure a boundary can collect — two bodies keeping a fee for one admission means the tier is taxed twice for the same body. A verdict cannot be produced by combat, because neither body will fight over the foot of a one-way stair; the instrument is one ruling from a named third body, read from standing it already owns. And a polity on this tier is a caretaker government staffed entirely by visitors, because the plains license plants and beasts and admit no humanoid, so a caretaker with no revenue is a queue nobody is obliged to keep. The asymmetry is the whole leverage: the watch may keep nothing, so it has nothing to lose, and the brokers keep everything, so they are judged on their own record. A Brinecaller is the only body that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, needs a shoreline, and is found on coasts and almost nowhere else.
history: Born on an estuary margin to two parents each trapped by their own element, which made her the biological answer to being trapped twice.
Was taught at nine to name the water she was standing in and was told by an adult that it was a party trick and then, an hour later, that it was a credential.
Dyed and cut as a road traveller at twenty, on the deliberate understanding that clothing is the only credential in the setting that costs nothing to verify.

Was charged twice at the Cairn Field in her thirty-first year — once by the ring's take and once by the broker's price — and produced two stamped slips that agreed in every particular except the amount.
Filed her first complaint at the gate and was told by the watch, correctly and without malice, that the watch could not read the broker's figure and had no standing to.
Learned the watch's own asymmetry in the third year of arguing and began using it: the watch may not keep a bead or a standing, so it loses nothing in a ruling, while the brokers keep everything.

Was offered a cultivation seat by three different houses over nine years and declined all three on the arithmetic, not the principle: a technique is a subscription, and she cannot stay anywhere long enough to be subscribed.
Filed the counter-petition in her fiftieth year, and has had it returned twice without a stated reason and once with a reason that contradicts the first two.

relationships.note: The watch keeps the order of the queue and has no jurisdiction on the plain, while the brokers sell what the order is worth, so the same arrival is sold once as a place and once as a price. Gate fees are the only tax ground that cannot measure a boundary can collect, which is why two bodies keeping a fee for one admission means the tier is taxed twice for the same body. She is the body in question, eighty times, and the two slips always agree except in the amount.

The only standing force on the plains, paid out of the ring's take and posted at the foot of the stair, existing because the only door out of a world that licenses nobody to enter fills with unlicensed arrivals. It may not keep a bead or a standing, so it has nothing to lose in a ruling and the brokers are judged entirely on their own record — which is the leverage she has spent twenty years pointing at, to a body that cannot act on it.

The brokers who sell standing at the Cairn Field, on the ground that no tier in the setting can produce a practitioner of its own, so gate fees are the only tax the plains can actually collect. They keep everything the take does not and are judged on their own record, which makes them the only party in the dispute with something to hide and the only one who has never had to answer for it.

A polity on this tier is a caretaker government staffed entirely by non-residents, because the plains admit no humanoid. A caretaker with no revenue is a queue nobody is obliged to keep, which is why nobody on the plains can simply stop charging — and why the only available dispute is about how many times one arrival may be sold, rather than about whether the fee exists.

The only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing a salt-adapted people with a fully watered one. It needs a shoreline and a shoreline is contested ground, so the cross spread along trade routes rather than across them — and she is the only courier on the tier who can be the same body on both sides of the one gate that taxes the crossing.

The Widow Run moved its bed and opened a crossing nobody surveyed, so two houses issuing at two crossings make the debt unpayable and the crossing uncitable. Her charge has moved with the river twice and been settled on a different foot both times, which is the strongest available evidence that the fee follows a queue rather than a body.

A traveller's cloth and cut say what they are and what they may open, because clothing is the only credential that costs nothing to verify. She had herself dyed to grade at twenty so that she would be permanently checkable at a gate, and has been — four hundred times, twice for each of the last eighty crossings.

One region, two incompatible reckonings, of which a contract's written calendar decides whether it can be disputed at all. Both halves of her double charge are written in different calendars, and the disagreement between them is why the two amounts differ rather than merely the duplication.

A count nobody can reconcile against the admissions actually issued. Eighty slips in a satchel is not a count, it is a sample, and she knows which of the two she is holding and has said so once to a clerk who wrote it down.

reference_stats.summary: Uncultivated, unremarkable in a fight, and very difficult to buy. What the record gives her is a chemical sense that reads two water chemistries at a glance and a body that crosses between them without harm, which on a tier whose only export is people is a commercial capability rather than a martial one.
strengths: reads brine and fresh water at a glance and can name which is in front of her, which is the best chemical sense in the setting
metabolises both chemistries without harm, so no single ration, well or shoreline can lock her out of a place
carries no technique and no subscription, so nothing can compel her, buy her, curse her or threaten her through qi
knows the gate-fee dispute better than either party and has eighty stamped slips that agree with each other
weaknesses: uncultivated by choice, so no gate, no technique, no reservoir and nothing that a cultivator could find
cannot remain anywhere long enough to cultivate, because a technique needs eleven consecutive periods and her work is one crossing
needs two chemistries within reach, so she is confined to coasts and is expensive to move inland

reference_stats.combat_read: There is nothing here for a cultivator and that is the correct reading. She cannot be suppressed, drained, sealed orQi-Suppressed, because she has nothing to suppress and nothing to take; and she is seventy-eight, gracile and untrained, so a competent body removes her from any engagement without effort. Do not read this as an absurdity: an uncultivated body on a tier where every technique is a subscription is the hardest person in the setting to threaten with qi and the easiest to simply walk past. If she must be stopped, stop the road.
notes: Her path is unaffiliated by arithmetic, not temperament, and the record must say so in her voice: a technique is a subscription and she has never spent eleven periods in one place.
The eighty slips are the load-bearing artefact. Do not let a scene resolve the toll cheaply — the prize cannot be split and the verdict must come from a named third body.
She is a carrier, not a combatant. Do not give her a combat gift.
